quarterly_data.signal: Power Integrations' 10-K names Lapis Semiconductor (ROHM Lapis Semiconductor Co., formerly OKI Electric Industry) and Seiko Epson Corporation, alongside X-FAB, as the three foundries that manufacture the vast majority of its silicon wafers using its proprietary high-voltage process technologies. The Lapis and Epson wafer supply agreements expire in December 2028 and December 2035; under each, the supplier has agreed to reserve a specified amount of production capacity and to sell wafers at fixed prices subject to periodic joint review, purchases are in U.S. dollars and yen/dollar exchange-rate fluctuations are shared equally. ICs are assembled, packaged and tested by independent subcontractors in China, Malaysia, Thailand and the Philippines; one subcontractor in Malaysia held approximately 16% of total property and equipment (excluding accumulated depreciation) in 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: Lapis agreement to December 2028, Epson agreement to December 2035 (capacity reserved, fixed prices); Malaysia subcontractor ~16% of total property and equipment (2025)

quarterly_data.signal: Power Integrations' 10-K contractual-obligations table shows purchase obligations of $45,121 (in thousands), all due in less than one year, representing commitments primarily for wafer and other inventory purchases, assembly and other manufacturing services, and purchases of property and equipment; at December 31, 2025 it had no non-cancelable purchase obligations due beyond one year.
quarterly_data.figure: Purchase obligations $45,121 thousand, all due within one year (wafers, inventory, assembly/manufacturing services, property and equipment)

connects_to.relationship: silicon wafer foundry manufacturing wafers on Power Integrations' proprietary high-voltage process technologies (wafer supply agreement with reserved production capacity)

contracts.signal: Power Integrations' 10-K names X-FAB Semiconductor Foundries AG as one of the three foundries it contracts with for the manufacture of the vast majority of its silicon wafers, using its proprietary high-voltage process technologies. Under the X-FAB wafer supply agreement, which expires in December 2028, X-FAB has agreed to reserve a specified amount of production capacity and to sell wafers at fixed prices subject to periodic joint review, and Power Integrations supplies rolling six-month forecasts on a monthly basis; purchases of wafers from X-FAB are denominated in U.S. dollars.
